text:
taylor: brain dump: proposal to implement a lightweight "slab shadow" layer so we can reassign ownership without moving big device buffers immediately. want quick thoughts on safety model and perf tradeoffs.
indra: define slab shadow? is that like an ownership indirection table that maps logical-tenant->physical-slab and can be updated atomically?
matt: yes. shadow = metadata that points to current owner and a residency state (HOT_ON_GPU, STAGED_HOST, DRAINING). moving ownership flips the shadow entry, not the buffer.
june: sounds attractive for avoiding memcpy, but how do kernels see the change? we still need a canonical pointer path.
taylor: idea: user-facing handles resolve via descriptor table: handle -> descriptor -> physical ptr. descriptors consult slab shadow for quick checks. changing owner updates descriptor ownership bit. existing kernels continue to use the physical ptr until they finish; new allocations from new owner go to other slabs.
indra: so no moving data, we just change accounting. that delays compaction but helps eviction/fairness fast-path. downside: fragmentation accumulates unless we compact later.
matt: we can combine: shadow swap for immediate ownership transfer + background consolidator that compacts low-utility fragments when system idle. the consolidator will migrate cold entries only.
june: correctness question: what about KV-cache pinned refs and direct device pointers used inside CUDA kernels? pinned refs must be respected. we cannot silently reassign ownership of slabs containing pinned device pointers.
taylor: agreed: slab-level flags: immutable_if_pinned. mark slab DRAINING prevents new pins; owner transfer is allowed only after pinned_count==0 or timeout. transfer still cheap because it's metadata-only.
indra: instrumentation: expose metric slab.shadow_transfers_total and slab.shadow_pending_transfers. run canary with transfer-only mode (no memcpy) and check p99 impact.
matt: edge case: dedicated/on-prem tenants that require physical isolation. controller policy should forbid shadowing for those tenants. map SLA->allow_shadowing boolean.
june: also add admin toggle that forces background_compaction.rate_limit so we don't thrash.
taylor: action items: 1) write a two-page design note describing slab shadow states and transition diagram (i'll take), 2) indra/matt prototype the descriptor indirection with atomic swap and metrics on dev, 3) june add policy flags and dashboard widgets.
mem-ops-bot: canary-job queued: slab-shadow-transfer-test (dev-tenant). ETA 2m.
indra: will watch canary metrics; focus on kv-cache pin churn and tail latencies.
matt: if canary is clean we can iterate on compactors later.
taylor: thanks all. small step: prefer metadata-only ownership change first, then add conservative background compaction later."
